title: Task Scheduler II
summary: Given an ordered array of task types and a minimum rest period between identical tasks, determine the least number of days required to complete all tasks, choosing each day to either perform the next task or take a break.
statement: Given an ordered array of task types and a minimum rest period between identical tasks, determine the least number of days required to complete all tasks, choosing each day to either perform the next task or take a break.
constraints: Tasks must be completed in their given order.
After performing a task type, at least space full days must pass before that type can run again.
Each day either performs the next task or is idle; return the earliest finishing day.
hints: Track the first legal future day for each task type.
For the next task, choose the later of the following calendar day and that task’s stored legal day.
After scheduling it, store current day + space + 1 as its next legal day.
Waiting longer can never help later ordered tasks, so choosing the earliest legal day greedily gives the minimum completion day.

tests.explanation: Tasks 1,2,1,2,3,1 can run on days 1,2,5,6,7,9, so nine days are required.
Run task 5 on day 1, task 8 on day 2, wait through days 3 and 4, then finish on days 5 and 6.
